en_US.title: Public Archive Contradiction Card
en_US.website_article:
A contradiction card is the archive refusing to smooth two facts into one clean sentence. It is used when a label and an object mark disagree, when a terminal receipt body points away from the header, when a claimant-safe line drops a witness hash, or when a route alias collides with a legal hold. The card keeps both facts visible and prevents the public archive from choosing the cleaner one because it is easier to print.

The card is not a verdict. It is a work order for doubt. One side may later fail. One side may only be a filing shortcut. Both sides may be true in different lanes: object custody, office custody, legal custody, and public category. Until proof order resolves the conflict, the contradiction card tells the reader what to test next.
en_US.wiki_article: Contradiction card: an archive object that pairs two evidence facts that cannot both be treated as final. The card must name both facts, the affected field, the reason code, the confidence state, and the next-proof target. It must not resolve final receiver, route consequence, protected claimant, Atlas consequence, or legal result.
en_US.pda_codex: PDA card: two facts disagree. Do not delete either line. Read the affected field, then follow proof order. If the object mark contradicts a label, test the object. If the receipt body contradicts the header, keep the body. If the claimant-safe line loses a witness hash, find the missing hash.
en_US.scanner_entry: Contradiction card available. Evidence facts conflict. Confidence: partial. Required next proof: object mark, receipt body, custody route, witness hash, or route alias.
en_US.terminal_note:
PUBLIC ARCHIVE CONTRADICTION CARD

Fact A retained.

Fact B retained.

Affected field recorded.

Do not merge into a clean label until proof order resolves the conflict.
en_US.evidence_caption: Contradiction card. The archive keeps two conflicting evidence facts visible and withholds the conclusion.
en_US.spoiler_policy: Contradiction-card language may appear early. Exact proof result, final receiver, protected claimant, Atlas consequence, legal result, and ending branch stay masked until later proof gates.
en_US.string_pool_key: Use hashed LocIDs in the Narrative layer. Keep scanner and PDA contradiction labels compact. Runtime must not parse this Markdown.

en_US.title: Claimant-Safe Redaction Audit Prompt
en_US.website_article:
Claimant-safe redaction is not a permission slip for silence. A public archive can hide a name and still show what kind of field was removed, whether a witness hash survived, whether the custody route changed, and whether the removal also made an office look cleaner. That is the audit line: protect the person, test the paperwork.

The audit does not reveal the claimant. It asks whether the omission changed the evidence route. If a summary removes a name but keeps the same object mark and witness hash, the redaction may be protective. If it removes a name, drops the hash, changes the receiver field, and pushes the packet into a legal hold, the archive has a contradiction to preserve.
en_US.wiki_article: Claimant-safe redaction audit: a procedure for reviewing protected omissions without exposing the claimant. The audit can list removed field type, reason code, surviving witness hash, custody-route effect, and next-proof target. It must not reveal claimant identity or final legal result.
en_US.pda_codex: PDA audit prompt: do not ask for the protected name first. Ask what field was removed. Check whether witness hash, custody route, object mark, and receiver field changed with it. If protection removed a person but also cleaned an office, keep the contradiction card open.

en_US.terminal_note:
CLAIMANT-SAFE REDACTION AUDIT

Protected name: locked.

Removed field type: required.

Witness hash state: required.

Custody route effect: required.

Do not expose claimant to test office liability.
en_US.evidence_caption: Redaction audit card. The archive keeps the protected name hidden while testing whether the omission changed the evidence route.

en_US.title: Route Alias Conflict Resolution Hint
en_US.website_article:
A route alias conflict starts when the old mark and the safe public label do not point cleanly at the same path. That does not make the alias false. HECTON-8 routes were renamed for claimant protection, office liability, salvage secrecy, and simple relay cleanup. The useful question is not which name sounds safer. The useful question is which name still matches the terminal path, scanner confidence, object custody, and receipt body.

The archive keeps the hint short because route names can spoil more than geography. An alias can reveal who moved a packet, who wanted the public name softened, or which route branch stayed alive after an office called it closed. The hint tells the reader what to compare and leaves the final route behind proof gates.
en_US.wiki_article: Route alias conflict: a condition where an old route mark and a public-safe route label disagree. Resolution should compare terminal receipt path, scanner confidence, custody route, route timestamp, and object mark. The conflict is not proof that either route is final.
en_US.pda_codex: PDA route hint: do not pick the safe label first. Compare old route mark, public route label, terminal receipt path, scanner downgrade reason, and custody route. If two names point to different proof targets, keep the family unresolved and follow the next-proof checklist.

Public label retained.

Compare terminal path, custody route, and scanner confidence before resolving route text.

Vergelijk terminalbonpad, scannervertrouwen, bewaringsroute, routetijd en objectmerk. De alias kan een persoon beschermen, een kantoor verbergen of alleen een relay opschonen. Houd finale routetekst vergrendeld.
